channel.title: The Temple News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Temple News (temple-news.com)

item.title: Temple Rome to offer four-year degrees
item.description: The Rome campus will offer eighteen different four-year undergraduate degrees from five Temple schools starting in the fall.

item.title: February 4: Lacrosse 2026 Begins
item.description: The Playbook is your way to get in the game for all things Temple Athletics. Join the TTN sports editors as they break down the past week in sports with expert analysis and appearances from some of your favorite Temple athletes.

item.title: Temple public safety staffing study calls for dozens of new officer hires
item.description: An independent staffing study released in December found Temple’s Department of Public Safety meets essential needs but lacks capacity for proactive policing.

item.title: Owls look to bounce back with more experience in 2026
item.description: Temple recorded just four wins last season, but is ready to put those shortcomings behind it and find success again.

item.title: Everyone should check in to “The Pitt”
item.description: A student reflects on HBO Max’s medical drama and the hope it can give audiences through hardship

item.title: “It got bad very quickly”: The rise and risks in college-aged online sports betting
item.description: Since the 2018 Supreme Court case Murphy v. National Collegiate Athletic Association, online sports betting has become commonplace in young Americans, especially at universities and colleges.

item.title: Second-half comeback leads Owls to win
item.description: Temple scored eight straight goals in the second half to take down Delaware 12-10 in the season opener.

item.title: Tobiason’s career-high leads Owls to win
item.description: Temple guard Aiden Tobiason scored a career-high 27 points in the 81-73 win against East Carolina Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Owls fall short to Mean Green
item.description: Temple committed 20 turnovers in its 69-66 loss to North Texas Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Jewish Voice for Peace investigated for September protest
item.description: The organization was placed on social probation following the university’s monthslong investigation into Student Conduct Code violations like excessive noise and identity concealment.
